title: Set 83

sentences.ko: 나 아홉 시까지 여기서 못 빠져나가면 막차 놓쳐. 그래서 8시 45분쯤부터 인사하고 다니려고. 나가는 길에 누가 나 붙잡고 말 못 걸게만 해 줘. 데이나네서 딱 그러다가 한 시간 더 있었거든.
sentences.text: If I don't get out of here by nine I'll miss the last train, so I'm going to start saying my goodbyes around a quarter to. Just don't let anybody pull me into a conversation on the way out, because that's exactly what happened at Dana's and I ended up staying another hour.

alts.text: I gotta be out of here by nine or I'm missing the last train, so I'm gonna start saying bye around quarter to. Just don't let anybody drag me into a conversation on my way out, cause that's exactly what happened at Dana's and I stayed another hour.

If I do not leave by nine, I will miss the last train, so I intend to begin saying my goodbyes at approximately a quarter to nine. Please do not allow anyone to draw me into a conversation on my way out, because that is precisely what happened at Dana's and I ended up staying another hour.

sentences.note: **a quarter to** 는 정각 15분 전을 가리킵니다. 아홉 시가 기준이니 8시 45분입니다. **pull me into a conversation** 는 나갈 참인데 누가 말을 걸어 붙잡아 두는 상황을 말합니다.
sentences.situation: 저녁 모임에서 먼저 일어날 구실 만들기

sentences.ko: 토요일에 네가 말해 준 그 집에 드디어 갔어. 빵은 네 말이 맞더라. 그 빵 하나 먹으러 또 갈 만해. 근데 그다음부터는 다 그냥 그랬달까? 나쁜 건 하나도 없었는데 네가 말한 그 밥은 아니었어. 내가 메뉴를 잘못 시켰나 봐.
sentences.text: So on Saturday we finally went to that place you told me about, and you were right about the bread, I'd honestly go back just for that. But everything after that was kind of fine? Nothing was bad, it just wasn't the meal you described. Maybe I ordered the wrong thing.

alts.text: Saturday we finally hit that place you told me about, and you were right about the bread, I'd honestly go back just for that. But everything after that was kinda just fine? Nothing was bad, it just wasn't the meal you described. Maybe I ordered the wrong thing.

On Saturday we finally visited the restaurant you recommended, and you were correct about the bread; I would honestly return for that alone. However, everything afterward was merely acceptable. Nothing was bad, it simply was not the meal you described. Perhaps I ordered the wrong dish.

sentences.note: **kind of fine** 은 나쁘지도 좋지도 않은 미지근한 평가입니다. 칭찬처럼 들리는 fine 앞에 kind of 를 붙이면 오히려 실망했다는 뜻이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 우리 집 개가 부엌 바닥 걸레질한 뒤로 거기를 무서워하기로 했나 봐. 바닥 끝에 서서 누가 안아서 건너편에 내려놓을 때까지 울어. 몸무게가 50파운드야. 그런데도 내가 계속 안아서 옮겨 주니까 이건 내 탓인 거 알아.
sentences.text: Our dog has decided he's scared of the kitchen floor ever since we mopped it, so he stands at the edge and cries until somebody carries him across. He's fifty pounds. And I keep carrying him anyway, so I know this is my fault.

alts.text: Ever since we mopped the kitchen floor, our dog's decided he's scared of it, so he stands at the edge crying till somebody hauls him across. He's fifty pounds. And I keep carrying him anyway, so I know this one's on me.

Our dog has decided that he is afraid of the kitchen floor ever since we mopped it, so he stands at the edge and cries until someone carries him across. He weighs fifty pounds. And I continue to carry him regardless, so I am aware that this is my own fault.

sentences.note: **has decided he's scared of** 는 개가 스스로 그렇게 정했다는 듯이 말해서 웃기게 만드는 표현입니다. **this one's on me** 는 이건 내 잘못이라는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 2월에 그 도자기 수업 신청해서 네 번 나갔어. 진짜 재미있기는 했어. 근데 화요일 일곱 시라 회사에서 곧장 가느라 저녁도 못 먹은 채였거든. 그래서 그냥 안 나가게 됐어. 앞치마는 아직 옷장 문에 걸려 있어. 봄에 다시 신청할 거라고 나한테 계속 말하고 있거든.
sentences.text: I signed up for that pottery class back in February and I made it to four classes, and I actually liked it, but it was Tuesdays at seven and I'd get there straight from work and I hadn't eaten. So I just stopped going. My apron's still hanging on the closet door because I keep telling myself I'll sign up again in the spring.

alts.text: That pottery class I signed up for back in February? I only got to four of them, and I really did like it, but it was Tuesdays at seven and I'd come straight from work and I hadn't eaten. So I just quit going. My apron's still on the closet door cause I keep telling myself I'll sign up again in the spring.

I enrolled in that pottery class in February and attended four classes, and I genuinely enjoyed it, but it was held on Tuesdays at seven and I would arrive directly from work without having eaten. So I simply stopped attending. My apron is still hanging on the closet door because I keep telling myself that I will enroll again in the spring.

sentences.note: **I made it to four classes** 는 겨우 네 번 나갔다는 뉘앙스입니다. make it to 는 어렵게 도달했다는 느낌이라 횟수가 적을 때 잘 씁니다. **straight from work** 는 회사에서 곧장 갔다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 우리 일요일마다 5번가 그 식당 갔었잖아. 그런데 가게를 싹 고쳤어. 이제 안이 환하고 앞에는 줄이 서 있고 우리 주문 외우던 그 아저씨도 없어. 그래도 좋아하고 싶어서 두 번이나 다시 가 봤어. 근데 지난번엔 자리에 앉고 나서 둘 다 딱히 거기 있고 싶지가 않더라.
sentences.text: We used to go to that diner on Fifth every Sunday, and then they redid the whole place, so now it's all bright and there's a line out front and the guy who knew our order is gone. I still want to like it, which is why we've been back twice. But we sat down last time and neither of us really wanted to be there.

alts.text: That diner on Fifth we used to go to every Sunday? They redid the whole place, so now it's all bright and there's a line out front and the guy who knew our order is gone. I still wanna like it, that's why we've been back twice. But last time we sat down and neither of us really wanted to be there.

We used to visit that diner on Fifth every Sunday, and then they renovated the entire place, so now it is very bright, there is a line outside, and the man who knew our order is no longer there. I still want to like it, which is why we have returned twice. But we sat down last time and neither of us truly wished to be there.

sentences.note: **used to** 는 지금은 안 하는 예전 습관을 말합니다. **redid the whole place** 는 가게를 통째로 새로 단장했다는 뜻이고, 인테리어를 갈아엎었다고 할 때 흔히 씁니다.

reviewed: 1번 formal 이 "at approximately a quarter to" 로 시각 없이 끝나 격식체에서 어색해서 "a quarter to nine" 으로 시각을 붙였습니다.
3번 note 가 별표로 감싼 he's decided he's scared of it 이 문장 안에 그대로 나오지 않아, 실제로 나오는 has decided he's scared of 로 고쳤습니다.
3번 formal 이 has become afraid 로 눅어져서 note 가 가르치는 "개가 스스로 그렇게 정했다" 는 농담이 사라졌습니다. has decided that he is afraid 로 되돌렸습니다.
4번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분(I signed up for ... back in February and I ... four classes)이 거의 같아서 도입을 바꿨습니다.
5번 casual 이 used to 를 빼고 "we hit every Sunday" 라는 지금도 다니는 말로 바뀌어 뜻이 달라졌고, note 가 가르치는 used to 도 사라져서 다시 넣었습니다.
4번 한국어 마지막 줄이 "신청하지 뭐, 하고 나한테 계속 그러고 있어서" 로 어순이 번역투라 자연스럽게 고쳤습니다.
